newsitem.title: USA: Musicland hires firm to explore options.
newsitem.headline: Musicland hires firm to explore options.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp said it hired the investment banking firm of Smith Barney "to explore all strategic and financial alternatives to improve the value of the company to its shareholders."
The company also said its bank group agreed to the terms of a plan that effectively waives all existing financial covenants through March 30, 1997.

Under the plan, the company said it has more financial flexibility during the fourth quarter. The covenant to pay down its revolver balance to $25 million for one day between December 15 and February 15, 1997, has been eliminated.
Instead, the new plan calls for the company to reduce its debt to $275 million by December 20 and to maintain that level through March 30, 1997, Musicland said.
The plan also permits the company to close additional underperforming stores.
"Given lower anticipated borrowing needs in 1997, the company and the bank group have additionally agreed to lower the overall maximum borrowing from $350 million to $300 million," the company said.
Musicland is a recorded music retailer.
